translations.answer: The project author does not need to provide explanations. Real-time deployment directly uses the global keypoint positions from the visual system output, as the strategy tracks sparse inputs (sparse inputs), not full-body motions (whole-body motions). The offline SMPL→H1 gradient retargeting is part of the training data preparation. The original thread did not publicly disclose the specific matrix transformation from RGB/HybrIK coordinates to Isaac Gym/robot world coordinates, so coordinate calibration still needs to be verified separately.
translations.applicability: Applies to the sparse tracking deployment design for human2humanoid/OmniH2O; the coordinate transformation and specific input format are not publicly disclosed in the original thread.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original author asked how to obtain processed AMASS-like joint data in real-time; the project author clarified that the deployment does not require a full-body reference.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between the offline whole-body motion tracking and the online sparse keypoint tracking, which are not the same input path.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Confirm that the real-time strategy consumes specific global keypoint positions, not the default reconstruction of full AMASS/SMPL motion.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Follow the project author's instructions, using global keypoint positions from Vision Pro or RGB+HybrIK as direct input to the real-time deployment, without repeating full-body motion retargeting in the real-time loop.
translations.details.environments.0: Human2humanoid/OmniH2O deployment context; Apple Vision Pro or RGB camera + HybrIK; original post did not provide software commit, frequency, or camera calibration parameters.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not answer the question about the specific matrix transformation, scale, origin, or time synchronization from RGB/HybrIK to Isaac Gym/robot world coordinates.
translations.details.limits.1: No public information on real-time deployment code, input tensor layout, or delay measurement, so it cannot be used to solely verify the real-time system.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The questioner replied that they now understand the difference between sparse input and whole-body retargeting.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Is it necessary to repeat the offline gradient retargeting of SMPL human data in real-time deployment in order to become a robot reference?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before real-time deployment, coordinate system, scale, timestamp, outlier keypoint filtering, and speed/position limits still need to be verified separately.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The offline SMPL→H1 retargeting process used for full-body training is mistakenly considered a mandatory step in the real-time sparse input deployment.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The user sees the training data preprocessing converting SMPL motion via gradient descent into H1 reference, thus not knowing how the real-time visual input meets the same interface.
